title: Dependency Management
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of dependency management and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—direct and transitive dependencies—in a small, readable example.
Identify one failure, compatibility, security, or resource-management concern and describe a safe response.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study dependency management with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you make builds and dependencies reproducible across developer machines and CI. In this lesson, focus on direct and transitive dependencies and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A reproducible build records dependencies, tool versions, and repeatable tasks. Keep environment-specific values out of source, and inspect transitive dependency changes rather than updating blindly. Apply that reasoning specifically to direct and transitive dependencies and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect direct and transitive dependencies with dependency versions before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Compare source files, dependencies, tests, and the artifact produced by the build. For ordinary Java SE examples, use JDK 25, save a complete class as Main.java, and run `javac Main.java` followed by `java Main`. CodeLeaf does not execute Java in the browser; use a local JDK for these examples. Preview-only and configuration-file examples have their own version or filename notes.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original example, remove any temporary output files it created, and rerun the baseline case. Do not leave credentials, generated private data, or large test files in the project directory.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.

content.task: Try it yourself: build the smallest program that demonstrates direct and transitive dependencies. Change one input, predict the result, and add one boundary or invalid case before considering the task complete.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates at least one listed topic from Dependency Management.
The learner states the expected result before running or inspecting the example.
At least one boundary, failure, compatibility, or maintainability consideration is documented where relevant.
hints: Start by identifying the contract or rule behind direct and transitive dependencies.
Reduce the example to the smallest input that makes the behavior visible.

content.execution_notes: Java requires a JDK or a separate isolated server runner. No Java sandbox is bundled with this content; never execute learner code inside the FastAPI process or public production container.

common_mistakes.problem: Applying the rule from memory without checking its exact contract.
common_mistakes.why: Small differences in type, scope, API version, or input shape can change the result.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the relevant official API/language documentation and build a minimal reproducer.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only a single happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Boundary values and failures often reveal assumptions hidden by the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add an empty, boundary, or invalid case and state the expected behavior before running it.

common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify the actual cause of a different result.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one factor at a time and keep a short record of observed behavior.

summary: Dependency Management is best understood by connecting its contract to a small observable example.
Key syllabus points: Direct and transitive dependencies, Dependency versions, Version conflicts.
Use official versioned documentation and tests to confirm assumptions before relying on behavior in a larger application.
